Subject: NovaClinic on-prem K8s: inventory & node/storage choices

Hi Anjali —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Per our discussion, I put together a short preflight to help us size node classes and pick a persistent volume strategy that matches your compliance needs. Can you confirm the following answers so we can move to a short design review?

- Total expected steady-state concurrent model workers: ~ (number)
- Peak concurrent inference sessions (per hour): ~ (number)
- Average request TTL / session length: (s)
- Any air-gapped / no-internet constraints for the cluster? (yes/no)
- Preferred storage backend: on-host NVMe, SAN (iSCSI), or NFS?
- KMS/HSM in-scope for key management? (vendor, e.g., AWS KMS, Thales)

I've attached a one-page preflight questionnaire to make the above quick to fill out. Once you've returned that, I'll loop in Neha and Laura to propose node pool sizes, IO class decisions, and a suggested encryption-at-rest profile.

Hiro Tanaka

Subject: Re: NovaClinic on-prem K8s: inventory & node/storage choices

Hiro —

Thanks, attached answers below inline and as a filled file. Apologies for being terse — juggling multiple sites this week.

- Steady-state model workers: ~24 (across 3 racks)
- Peak inference sessions: ~160 per hour (spiky weekdays)
- Avg session length: 3–10s for short requests, some multi-step flows ~45s
- Air-gap: No; however outbound egress is heavily filtered and must go through our proxy for telemetry
- Storage: We prefer local NVMe for hot model shards and a SAN (iSCSI) for larger persistent volumes. NFS for shared config only.
- KMS: We use an on-prem Thales HSM for key material; can provide admin contacts.

We also have a constraint: all model artifacts >2GB must stay on-site and not be staged in public S3.

Attached: preflight_answers_filled.docx

Best,
Anjali
IT Director, NovaClinic

Hi team —

Thanks Anjali for the quick answers — that's very helpful. Based on the inputs, here are our initial recommendations (high level) before we schedule a design review:

1) Node pool topology
- Controller/control plane: 3x m6i-equivalent (or baremetal small VMs), isolated management VLAN, no GPU.
- Model-serving GPU pool: 8x A100-equivalent nodes in a dedicated node pool (taints: redwood=serving:NoSchedule), split across the 3 racks for failure domain separation. Plan for 1 spare GPU host for N+1.
- Model-shard hot storage nodes: 6x NVMe-only nodes (local-block PVs) attached to the model-serving pool as sidecar storage for low-latency shard reads. Use a CSI driver with local PVs (example: local-static-provisioner).
- Batch/async worker pool: 6x CPU-only nodes, autoscaling group; spot/preemptible equivalent is OK if you accept job restarts.

2) PV strategy and IO
- Hot weights (models <2GB shards): local NVMe on model-serving nodes. Keep anti-affinity rules to avoid colocation of replicas on same host.
- Large artifacts (>2GB): provision LVM-backed iSCSI volumes from your SAN; use a CSI driver supporting ReadWriteOnce for model downloads.
- Shared config: small NFS export mounted read-only into pods for static manifests.

3) Encryption & keys
- Integrate Redwood's key-wrapping with your Thales HSM via KMIP if available; if not, a hardened KMS proxy in the management VLAN.

4) Network & egress
- Outbound telemetry must go via your proxy — we will provide a proxy configuration snippet for the agent and sidecars.

5) Canary & rollout plan (brief)
- Canary 1: single node in rack A serving synthetic traffic for 48 hours.
- Canary 2: 10% traffic across two racks, validate latency and error quotas.

I've attached a short note with PV tradeoffs and recommended CSI drivers. Also linking a one-page runbook template we use for on-prem onboarding.

Attachments: [Attachment: pv-recommendations.pdf (pdf, 72KB)], [Attachment: redwood-runbook-template.md (md, 6KB)]

Next step: Hiro — can you set up a 45-minute design review with Anjali + their ops contact and include a short inventory of rack topology (U positions, switch uplinks, storage fabric endpoints)?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NovaClinic on-prem K8s: inventory & node/storage choices

Hiro / Laura —

Appreciate the plan. A couple of constraints from our side (ops):
- SAN iSCSI controllers are currently oversubscribed; we'd prefer using local NVMe for any read-heavy model shards and only pull large artifacts onto iSCSI during off-peak windows.
- Network: all intra-rack east-west traffic should be on a private VXLAN overlay; mgmt VLAN will be L3-restricted.
- We need a step-by-step runbook for the model rollout and a rollback path (including how to evacuate ephemeral NVMe caches).

Attached a topology sketch and a short bullet list of maintenance windows.

Attachments: [Attachment: site-topology.png (png, 210KB)]

Anjali / EdgeCorp Ops —

Thanks for the quick replies and the topology sketch. Summarizing the agreed action items so we can lock a date for the design review (proposed Wed 2027-04-28 10:00 ET):

1) NovaClinic to provide: full rack inventory (U positions, switch ports, iSCSI controllers + zoning), maintenance windows for non-disruptive testing — due 2027-04-23.
2) Redwood to provide: detailed nodeclass sizing doc (CPU/GPU/memory), CSI driver compatibility matrix, and a runbook that includes NVMe cache evacuation steps — draft due 2027-04-25.
3) Joint design review: 45-minute meeting to validate canary steps, egress/proxy config, and HSM keyflow — target 2027-04-28.
4) Post-review: pilot (single rack) for 2 weeks with synthetic load; fallback to sandbox cluster if errors exceed thresholds.

Links: design folder — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X_example_novaclinic_onprem
